question.text: A source of light is placed in front of a screen. The intensity of light on the screen is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math>. Two Polaroids <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> are so placed in between the source of light and screen that the intensity of light on the screen is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>I</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. Then the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>, should be rotated by an angle of (degrees) so that the intensity of light on the screen becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>I</mi></mrow><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math>.

solution.text:
Recall the law of Malus I'=I2cos2θ

Here θ is the angle between two polaroids, 

⇒3I8=I2cos2θ⇒θ=30°.
